solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Raised voices: Posh half cut on seaside jaunt?

indicators.note: cutting a word in half leaves its back two letters here, so only the second half of Posh is kept

parts.note: an outing is a pleasure trip, such as a day at the seaside

explanation.surface: Someone well-to-do, a bit tipsy on a trip to the coast, getting loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half cut' looks like British slang for tipsy describing the posh person; here it tells you to lose half of the word Posh, leaving SH.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouting, as a noun, is the sound of people raising their voices in loud speech.

clue.text: Tired MI6 man devouring fish on way back

indicators.note: the spy eats up the reversed fish, so it goes inside

parts.note: MI6 is the British secret intelligence service, so its man is a spy

indicators.note: the fish comes back the other way, read right to left

parts.note: an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A weary British secret agent eating fish on his way home.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepy means drowsy, ready for bed, close to tired.

clue.text: Couturier exposed by assembly man

parts.note: outed, made public; out
a fitter is someone who assembles machinery

explanation.surface: A fashion designer revealed by a factory worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A seller or maker of clothing, so a fashion designer is a fair stand-in.

clue.text: Conclude changing leader is a provocation

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for conclude is swapped for another

parts.note: to conclude is to end, to cease

explanation.surface: Ending a change of party leader is said to stir trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: The C of CEASE is replaced by T; the clue does not say which letter comes in, only that the leader changes.
explanation.definitionFit: A tease is a remark or act meant to provoke or taunt someone playfully.

clue.text: Miser moving slowly along, briefly upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the letters read backwards
briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: dragging, as in feet dragging

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted person shuffling along, briefly troubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' cuts DRAGGING to DRAGGIN, and 'upset' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A niggard is a stingy, mean person, one who hoards money.

clue.text: One letting off steam in police pen?

definitions.meaning: a pot for boiling water that whistles as steam escapes
kettling is the police tactic of penning protesters into a confined area; the cordon itself is so called

explanation.surface: A protester venting anger while hemmed in by police lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A boiler for water releases steam, and a police cordon penning a crowd is also called by this name.

clue.text: Clear one interrupting former judge

indicators.note: one breaks into the middle of the other letters, as a heckler interrupts

parts.note: ex means former
to rate is to judge or assess
taken as written

explanation.surface: A court scene: someone cuts in on a retired judge to acquit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' looks like a noun but is the verb rate.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear of blame or guilt, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Evidence of ghetto Kenya largely erased

indicators.note: most of the two words is rubbed out, leaving only a short run from their middle

explanation.surface: Signs of a deprived quarter of Kenya have mostly been wiped away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Largely erased' strips 'ghet' and 'ya' from the two words, leaving the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: A token of something is a sign or proof of it, as a token of goodwill.

clue.text: Threaten corrupt grandee? Not at first

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or twisted, so the letters are rearranged
at first takes only the opening letter of Not

explanation.surface: Does a bent aristocrat pose a danger? Supposedly not, initially.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not at first' seems to deny the threat; it supplies N, which joins GRANDEE in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To endanger is to put at risk, which is to threaten harm.

clue.text: Alienate holy man in eastern mountains

indicators.note: the holy man is placed in among the letters for eastern and mountains

parts.note: a range is a chain of mountains
ST, short for saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A monk retreating to remote eastern peaks, cutting himself off from others.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate someone is to turn them away, make them distant and unfriendly; a verb synonym.

clue.text: Addicted, as Sturgeon may be?

definitions.meaning: unable to give something up, caught by a habit
a sturgeon is a fish, which an angler catches on a hook

explanation.surface: Pokes fun at Nicola Sturgeon, former Scottish First Minister, as if hooked on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being caught on a habit is like a fish caught on a line, so addiction and angling share the word.

clue.text: Naked bishop about to embrace one?

indicators.note: the bishop and about hug the letter for one between them

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
re means about, concerning
a, the indefinite article, means one

explanation.surface: A bishop with no clothes about to hug someone: a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means without covering or clothes, so unclothed and naked agree.

clue.text: Model draped around me? That's Grace

indicators.note: the model's pose is wrapped round the letter for me, as cloth is draped round a figure

parts.note: to model is to pose, as for an artist
I, the speaker's word for me

explanation.surface: An artist's model in fabric asks whether she embodies elegance.
explanation.definitionFit: Poise is composed, graceful bearing, so grace in movement is a fair synonym.

clue.text: A married man gone abroad to fight at Troy

definitions.text: A married man gone abroad to fight at Troy

indicators.note: abroad here in the sense of all over the place, so the letters are scattered

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for married, as on forms

explanation.surface: Describes the Greek king who left his wife Clytemnestra to lead the siege of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' seems to be part of the story, a man going overseas, but it signals that A, M, MAN and GONE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mycenaean king led the Greek army to Troy and was husband of Clytemnestra, so the whole clue describes him.

clue.text: Wait on American minister nursing temperature

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the American minister holds the temperature within

parts.note: to minister to someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A US clergyman looking after a patient running a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minister' looks like a noun, a clergyman, but works as the verb, to tend.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend someone is to serve or look after them, as a servant waits on a master.

clue.text: Delete a timeline that's inaccurate

indicators.note: inaccurate means wrong, so the letters come out wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: An instruction to strike out a flawed chronology.
explanation.definitionFit: To eliminate something is to remove or get rid of it, as to delete text.

clue.text: Warning for wife that was large

parts.note: a former wife is an ex
ample means large or plentiful

explanation.surface: A cautionary tale about a former spouse who used to be big.
explanation.definitionFit: A punishment made an example of serves as a warning to others, so the two can stand for each other.

clue.text: Puts on rubbish suit, type favoured by Rees-Mogg

parts.note: pins, as when one pins on a badge
tripe means nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Someone dons a dreadful suit of the sort a fusty Tory MP might wear.
explanation.walkthrough: Jacob Rees-Mogg is a British Conservative politician known for his old-fashioned double-breasted suits.
explanation.definitionFit: A suit cloth with thin vertical lines, the formal look of bankers and traditional politicians.

clue.text: Bird that might be presented to you at Jimmy Choo's?

definitions.meaning: a large African stork-like wading bird with a huge clog-shaped beak

definitions.text: might be presented to you at Jimmy Choo's
definitions.meaning: Jimmy Choo is a luxury shoe brand, so its customers are handed the invoice for footwear

explanation.surface: Asks which bird a shopper might be handed at a designer footwear store.
explanation.definitionFit: The name is both an African bird with a shoe-shaped beak and, split in two, a footwear invoice.

clue.text: One hounding prince, you say — and his mum?

indicators.note: you say signals that the prince's name is given as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: Prince Harry
his mum would be her, which a dropped-H speaker would pronounce 'er

explanation.surface: A query whether a royal and his mother are hunting someone down, perhaps the press.
explanation.walkthrough: The ER comes from 'her' with its H dropped, the way a Cockney might refer to someone's mother.
explanation.definitionFit: A harrier is a hound bred for hunting hares, and also anyone who harasses, so one hounding fits.

clue.text: Look after one's bottom

definitions.meaning: to bring up, as of children or livestock

explanation.definitionFit: To rear children is to raise and care for them; the rear is also the buttocks.

clue.text: Making out with Carol, dropping some Es

indicators.note: the Es are dropped into the middle of the carol, as one drops something into a container

parts.note: to carol is to sing joyfully
a couple of the letter E

explanation.surface: A racy scene: kissing with someone called Carol while taking ecstasy pills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making out' suggests kissing and 'Es' ecstasy tablets; here 'making out' means discerning, and the Es are just letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something out is to perceive it with the eyes, so discerning and seeing are synonyms.

clue.text: Little mark left by wound, but very red?

parts.note: a scar is the mark left when a wound heals
-let is a suffix meaning little, as in piglet or booklet

explanation.surface: A small wound mark that is nonetheless vividly coloured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little' supplies the diminutive ending -LET, so a little scar is read as a scar-let.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarlet is a brilliant red hue, a strong shade of red.

clue.text: Applauds revolutionary society locking up Her Maj

indicators.note: the revolutionary society imprisons the queen inside its letters

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Marxist revolutionary
Her Majesty the Queen, ER for Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A rebel group imprisoning the monarch, and someone clapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheers, as a verb, means shouts approval, which is applauding.

clue.text: Cook a nice dhal? Diners might enjoy it

indicators.note: to cook is to doctor or rework, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A suggestion to prepare an Indian lentil dish for restaurant guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' sits naturally with the dhal recipe, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A filled tortilla of Mexican cuisine is a dish that restaurant customers eat, so the definition describes it loosely.

clue.text: Steps taken to deceive a heartless geisha

parts.note: to con is to deceive

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle, leaving only the outside letters of geisha

explanation.surface: Moves made to trick a Japanese entertainer who lacks compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' seems to describe a cruel geisha; it keeps just G and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A conga is a dance done in a line, so its sequence of steps stands for it.

clue.text: A longing often unexpressed by East Ender

parts.note: an itch is a restless desire, a longing

explanation.surface: A craving that a Londoner from the East End seldom voices.
explanation.walkthrough: East Enders, Cockney Londoners, famously drop the H sound at the start of words.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the spoken name of the letter H, which Cockney speech commonly leaves silent.

clue.text: Crime of a penniless priest

indicators.note: without the penny, whose abbreviation is P

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman

explanation.surface: Asks what offence a destitute clergyman might commit.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the criminal act of deliberately setting fire to property.

clue.text: Ancient Greek edition I analysed in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A scholar mentions a classical text in a version they studied.
explanation.definitionFit: Ionians were one of the main tribes of the ancient Hellenes, settled in Asia Minor and Attica.

clue.text: A lot of specially ground Jamaica pepper

indicators.note: pepper is ground in a mill, and here the letters are ground up and rearranged
a lot of a word but not all of it, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A cook grinding a large amount of a Caribbean spice in a special way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot of' takes SPECIALL from 'specially', and 'ground' turns those letters into the spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Jamaica pepper is another name for the dried berry of the pimento tree, used as a spice.

clue.text: Rich Liberal provoked, losing head

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for provoked is lost

parts.note: goaded means provoked or prodded

explanation.surface: A wealthy Liberal politician, needled, flying off the handle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Losing head' hints at losing one's temper; it removes the first letter of GOADED.
explanation.definitionFit: Loaded is informal for very wealthy, having plenty of money.

clue.text: Pudding problem at Johnson's alma mater?

parts.note: Boris Johnson went to Eton College
a mess is a difficult situation, a problem

explanation.surface: Mocks the troubles traced to Boris Johnson's old school.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is the elite English boarding school attended by Boris Johnson; ETON MESS is a dessert of strawberries, cream and meringue.
explanation.definitionFit: The dish of crushed meringue, cream and berries is a classic British dessert, served after the main course.
